_comment: Funders spotted but not yet watched. Two ways in: the daily sweep meets a funder through an aggregator that is not in sources.json, and a weekly pass searches for newly launched funds. Nothing here reaches the site. A candidate becomes a source only when a person moves it into sources.json — an automated list that adds its own sources would eventually add a scam, and the only thing this site has is being trustworthy.

candidates.name: California Civic Media Program
candidates.why: Public-private fund (State of California matched by Google, $20M total) making one-time grants of up to $250,000 to California news organizations for original reporting and civic engagement, with an emphasis on underserved local communities.
candidates.evidence: Governor's office announcement, gov.ca.gov, 14 Jul 2026, and the program's own page at business.ca.gov/california-civic-media-program/; application window closed 21 Aug 2026, with Journalism Funding Partners and the James B. McClatchy Foundation administering the two halves. Read October 2026.

candidates.name: Stimuleringsfonds voor de Journalistiek (SVDJ / Dutch Journalism Fund)
candidates.why: Dutch government-backed independent fund running recurring grant schemes (the SVDJ Accelerator, investigative-journalism collaborations, local-journalism innovation and professionalization) open to journalists and newsrooms in the Netherlands.
candidates.evidence: svdj.nl's own programme pages and business.gov.nl's 'Dutch journalism subsidies' overview, describing active 2026 grant rounds; financed by the Ministry of Education, Culture and Science. Read October 2026.

candidates.name: National Institute for Health Care Management (NIHCM) Foundation
candidates.why: Funds annual US health-care journalism grants of $15,000-$30,000 for independent journalists and newsrooms.

candidates.name: Media Innovation Europe (International Press Institute consortium)
candidates.why: Funds European media organisations' audience-engagement and business-innovation projects.

candidates.name: Henry Nxumalo Foundation / SA|AJP
candidates.why: Provides investigative-journalism reporting grants and editorial support to journalists and newsrooms across the SADC region.

candidates.name: Batory Foundation / EEA & Norway Grants Civil Society Fund Poland
candidates.why: Administers Polish civil-society grants including calls for projects countering disinformation, some of which fund media literacy/journalism activity.

candidates.name: Tech Policy Press
candidates.why: Funds a $10,000, year-long fellowship for journalists, researchers and policy professionals reporting on tech and democracy.

candidates.name: Exile Hub
candidates.why: Runs the Critical Voices Fellowship and other emergency/production funds for exiled Myanmar media professionals.

candidates.name: Durham University - Sir Harry Evans Memorial Fund
candidates.why: Nine-month early-career investigative journalism fellowship placed inside a Reuters newsroom.

candidates.name: Nova Institute for Health
candidates.why: Funds a $60,000 annual Nova Media Fellowship for health journalism; grants.json previously recorded the funder under the shorthand name "Nova Media", now corrected.

candidates.name: Walkley Foundation
candidates.why: Australian journalism foundation that co-administers and hosts grant programmes for freelance journalists.

candidates.name: Fundación Avina
candidates.why: Latin American foundation that co-funds Fundación Gabo's investigative-journalism grants on sustainable-development themes.

candidates.name: The Climate Pledge
candidates.why: Co-funds, with the National Geographic Society, storytelling grants (up to $100,000) for journalists and other storytellers covering climate resilience, energy transition and sustainability.

candidates.name: Fulbright-National Geographic Digital Storytelling Fellowship (via Fulbright/IIE)
candidates.why: A joint Fulbright/National Geographic award funding US citizens to combine an academic research grant abroad with digital storytelling/multimedia journalism training.

candidates.name: Reflecta Fördermittelkompass
candidates.why: A German funding database that aggregates media/journalism grant and scholarship listings not otherwise indexed by the existing aggregator sources.

candidates.name: Africa No Filter
candidates.why: Runs the Voices for Climate Justice Program, an adjacent-track grant explicitly open to journalists producing climate-justice content in ten African countries.

candidates.name: German Embassy Kyiv
candidates.why: Funds a recurring Ukrainian human-rights project call with a press/media-freedom and disinformation priority area, restricted to Ukrainian media organisations.

candidates.name: Society of Professional Journalists (SPJ) Foundation
candidates.why: US journalism nonprofit's foundation running an annual grant cycle for journalists/newsrooms plus a small members-only Freelance Fund mini-grant.

candidates.name: Media Diversity Institute (Western Balkans)
candidates.why: Runs journalism-adjacent media literacy/gender programmes in the Western Balkans (currently the MLADI Award, a prize, so not recorded as a grant); may run other applicable funding.

candidates.name: Public Interest Journalism Lab (PIJL)
candidates.why: Runs an emergency/operational grants programme (several open calls per year, plus a 2026 scholarship call with ECPMF) for Ukrainian regional media outlets and individual journalists, prioritising frontline regions.

candidates.name: The Fix Media Foundation — Technology Support Fund
candidates.why: Runs an equipment grant scheme replacing lost or outdated gear for journalists working in frontline or high-risk areas in Ukraine/Eastern Europe. Note: a separate URL from the already-tracked 'thefix.media' source (The Fix media innovation programmes) — may be a related but distinct foundation entity worth checking.

candidates.name: The Lenfest Institute for Journalism
candidates.why: Runs its own journalism funding programmes (e.g. Lenfest-Google News Initiative News Catalyst Grants for local news community-listening projects) beyond the Google co-branded one.

candidates.name: African Investigative Journalism Conference (AIJC)
candidates.why: Runs an annual, francophone-focused, fully-funded conference fellowship for investigative journalists in Africa.

candidates.name: Harold W. McGraw, Jr. Center for Business Journalism
candidates.why: Runs a recurring (spring/fall) $15,000 business-journalism reporting fellowship open to freelance and staff journalists.

candidates.name: Journalism Science Alliance
candidates.why: EJC-hosted, EUR 2.7 million, two-year programme (2025-2027) delivering grant funding, training, mentoring and networking for science-backed investigative journalism; annual call cycle, currently closed for 2026.

candidates.name: International Fund for Public Interest Media (IFPIM)
candidates.why: Global multilateral fund making grants up to US$250,000 to independent public-interest media organisations in low- and middle-income countries across Africa, the Middle East, Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Eastern Europe.
candidates.evidence: ifpim.org and gfmd.info funding archive; IFJ (ifj.org) press release, 1 Aug 2026, on the IFPIM-funded $1m Palestine media fund it distributes through the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: RCDIJ Africa Fund (Ripples Centre for Data and Investigative Journalism)
candidates.why: Nigeria-based nonprofit's pan-African fund of up to US$10,000 for individual journalists' data and investigative journalism projects.
candidates.evidence: Media Rights Agenda (mediarightsagenda.org) and gfmd.info funding-archive coverage of the 2026 RCDIJ Africa Fund call; confirmed on rcdij.org. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: St. David's Foundation
candidates.why: Central Texas health foundation funding local newsrooms and community-centered journalism covering health and social issues affecting underserved communities, through its 'Strengthening Local Media to Advance Community Health' programme.
candidates.evidence: stdavidsfoundation.org 2026 grantmaking announcement naming 21 organisations awarded over $3m under the local-media funding opportunity. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: Journalists for Human Rights (JHR)
candidates.why: Canadian media-development NGO training journalists in 23 countries to report on human rights, democratic reform and climate, with small reporting grants available to journalists who complete its training.
candidates.evidence: opportunitiesforyouth.org write-up of the 2026 JHR Program; re-seen today via the GFMD funding feed (Gordon N. Fisher / JHR Fellowship listing).

candidates.name: Solutions Journalism Network
candidates.why: Co-runs journalism fellowships with other funders (e.g. the European media leaders climate solutions fellowship with EJC) and posts fellowship calls on its own site.

candidates.name: European Media and Information Fund (EMIF)
candidates.why: Gulbenkian-hosted fund running open calls for media literacy, disinformation research and journalism-adjacent projects across Europe; surfaced while researching the EEA Grants Romania disinformation call. Not verified in depth — flagged for a future dedicated check.

candidates.name: Alfred Friendly Press Partners
candidates.why: Runs a six-month fellowship placing early-career journalists (aged 25-35, 3+ years' experience) from developing countries in U.S. newsrooms via the Missouri School of Journalism, with a $2,000 living stipend and essentials covered, plus a separate four-week programme for journalists living in exile in the US. Surfaced as a Scholars at Risk 'Practitioners at Risk' host-institution partner.

candidates.name: Digital Forensic Research Lab (DFRLab), Atlantic Council
candidates.why: Runs Digital Sherlocks, a free annual training programme for journalists/civil society on monitoring and protecting the information environment, listed as a media opportunity via IJNet.

candidates.name: Climate Justice Resilience Fund (CJRF)
candidates.why: Explicitly funds documentation, journalism, oral histories and visual storytelling as part of its climate-justice grantmaking to frontline communities — a much closer match to the 'climate-justice-resilience' source's own name and stated purpose than the currently configured ClimateWorks Foundation URL, which is invitation-only and unrelated to media. Worth tracking as its own source.

candidates.name: FRIDA — The Young Feminist Fund
candidates.why: Global feminist fund listed on Global Fund for Women's own funder-resources page; young-feminist-led groups doing storytelling/media work could plausibly fit the adjacent track.

candidates.name: Equality Fund
candidates.why: Global feminist funder running its own Global Journalism Fellowship 2026-2027 (CAD 4,000/USD 4,000 reported inconsistently, five fellows from ODA-recipient countries), in partnership with CJFE and AWiM.

candidates.name: AmplifyChange
candidates.why: Funder of sexual and reproductive rights advocacy listed on Global Fund for Women's funder-resources page; advocacy-communications grants may be adjacent-track eligible.

candidates.name: Africa Women's Development Fund (AWDF)
candidates.why: Pan-African feminist fund listed on Global Fund for Women's funder-resources page; not yet assessed for media/documentation eligibility.

candidates.name: Joan Shorenstein Fellowship Program (Shorenstein Center, Harvard Kennedy School)
candidates.why: A one-year (mostly remote) fellowship for journalists with 10+ years' experience to research public policy/political affairs at Harvard; surfaced during today's gijn-grants search fallback.

candidates.name: Press Forward
candidates.why: A $500M+ philanthropic collaborative funding U.S. local news outlets directly (e.g. its 2025 Open Call awarded ~$100k each to 200+ small newsrooms); it also co-funds IWMF's Safety Ambassador Fellowship, and its own Pooled Fund/Open Call cycles could be a distinct grant source worth tracking.

candidates.name: UN Trust Fund to End Violence against Women and Girls (UNTF)
candidates.why: The actual grant-making body behind UN Women's largest civil-society calls for proposals (four-year core/flexible grants, up to ~USD 20M per round across two cohorts) — a more useful source URL than sources.json's current un-women procurement page, which is for vendor procurement, not grants.

candidates.name: Kosovar Civil Society Foundation (KCSF)
candidates.why: Co-manages the Civic Emergency Fund with Trag Foundation and runs its own recurring 'Urgent Grants' open call for Kosovo/regional civil society, which may independently be usable by media/journalism organisations under threat.

candidates.name: Climate Tracker
candidates.why: Runs recurring regional climate-journalism fellowships/reporting grants (e.g. a Latin America solutions-journalism fellowship, stipend up to US$1,000, deadline 16 Feb 2026) surfaced via Terra Viva Grants; not currently open, no entry added, but worth tracking as its own source.

candidates.name: British Council Serbia
candidates.why: UK-Serbia arts/culture co-creation grants (up to GBP 15,000) surfaced while researching the British Embassy Belgrade funding landscape; a distinct funder from the Embassy itself and not currently tracked as its own source.

candidates.name: Digital Whistleblowing Fund (Hermes Center / Renewable Freedom Foundation)
candidates.why: Micro-grants of up to €3,000 plus IT/advisory support for investigative-journalism groups and human-rights grassroots organisations starting secure digital whistleblowing initiatives, requiring endorsement by a partner such as ICIJ, OCCRP or Transparency International.
candidates.evidence: Listed on GIJN's grants & fellowships resource page (surfaced via WebSearch since gijn.org returned HTTP 403 today); most corroborating search results date to ~2020, so current-cycle status is uncertain. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: CTRL+J
candidates.why: Runs Luminate-backed microgrants (US$1,000-5,000) for small convenings on journalism and technology, plus a separate Research Hub for Global South researchers; not yet in sources.json.

candidates.name: CIJI — Collaborative and Investigative Journalism Initiative
candidates.why: EU-funded consortium (partner: Free Press Unlimited) coordinating cross-border investigative journalism grant calls, e.g. the 2026 'cross-border investigations on the impact of AI' grants; may run further calls independently of Free Press Unlimited's own listing.

candidates.name: E3J — European Excellence Exchange in Journalism
candidates.why: EU-funded project (partner: Free Press Unlimited) that has run small production-grant calls (e.g. EUR 10,000 grants for cross-border stories on climate, migration and public health); last known round closed September 2024, current cycle status unconfirmed.

candidates.name: Sudan Media Forum (SMF)
candidates.why: Coalition of independent Sudanese media outlets that jointly launches funding calls with Free Press Unlimited (e.g. 2026 content-production retainers of EUR 1,000 each for 60 individual journalists); worth watching as a co-administering body even though it is not itself the primary funder.

candidates.name: Mongabay
candidates.why: Environmental-journalism nonprofit that co-funds One World Media's Amazon Film Grant (up to $5,000 for documentaries on the Amazon rainforest ecosystem) and may run its own independent journalism-funding programmes.

candidates.name: CITE (Centre for Innovation and Technology, Zimbabwe)
candidates.why: Runs an annual investigative-journalism grants call (up to US$800 per story) for journalists reporting on Zimbabwean communities.

candidates.name: Minor Foundation for Major Challenges (MFMC)
candidates.why: Norwegian foundation funding climate-communication projects specifically (public opinion/attitude change/information campaigns), profiled on the Terra Viva Grants directory; recurring, multi-round-per-year funder with a genuine media/documentation angle.

candidates.name: Slovak Agency for International Development Cooperation (SlovakAid) — Small Grants Serbia
candidates.why: Bilateral-embassy-style small-grants programme (up to €10,000, civil society/governance themes) surfaced while researching UK Embassy Belgrade funding, similar in shape to the AU/US/UK embassy sources already tracked but not itself in the registry.

candidates.name: EU Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme (CERV)
candidates.why: A distinct EU funding programme from Creative Europe; its CERV-2026-CITIZENS-CIV-ENGAGEMENT-DISINFOFIMI topic funds citizen-engagement work countering disinformation/FIMI (EUR 10M sub-budget), though its own eligible-applicant language does not clearly name news media as a target group — worth judging as an adjacent-track source on its own terms in a future sweep.

candidates.name: Media Foundation for West Africa (MFWA)
candidates.why: West African press-freedom NGO that just launched a GHS 544,000 Legal Support Fund giving journalists and media organisations in Ghana legal representation against SLAPPs and other litigation, under its EU-funded Africa Media Integrity and Resilience Programme (also active in Ethiopia and the Central African Republic).
candidates.evidence: IFEX (ifex.org) and MFWA's own site (mfwa.org/issues-in-focus) announcing the Legal Support Fund on 17 September 2026, corroborated by allAfrica, Ghana Business News and MyJoyOnline coverage the same week. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: Fonds Bijzondere Journalistieke Projecten (Fonds BJP)
candidates.why: Dutch independent foundation (est. 1990, partly government-supported) that grants direct subsidies to journalists and authors for articles, longreads, journalistic books, documentaries and podcasts published or broadcast in Dutch, including a recurring grant round specifically for journalists in the Caribbean part of the Kingdom.
candidates.evidence: Curacao Chronicle (curacaochronicle.com) report on the fund's second 2026 Caribbean grant round, corroborated by the fund's own site fondsbjp.nl. Read September 2026.

candidates.name: Official Development Assistance (ODA) Germany Grants
candidates.why: Listed as a distinct funding item on EJC's funding roundup page (status: Applications closed), a separate funder from EJC/IJ4EU with no tracked source of its own; no own-site URL was given in the snapshot.

candidates.name: Black Sea Trust for Regional Cooperation (German Marshall Fund)
candidates.why: Runs recurring calls for proposals and travel grants strengthening civil society and regional cooperation across the Black Sea region (Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Moldova, Romania, Türkiye, Ukraine) — squarely in OIP's own beat but not currently tracked.

candidates.name: European Fact-Checking Standards Network (EFCSN)
candidates.why: Runs 'Innovation Grants' funding technical tools and disinformation interventions for European fact-checking organisations — a direct media/verification funder in the information-integrity space OIP covers, missing from the registry.

candidates.name: Stanley Center for Peace and Security
candidates.why: Co-runs the COP31 Climate Change Media Partnership Reporting Fellowship jointly with Internews Earth Journalism Network.

candidates.name: The GroundTruth Project
candidates.why: Runs the James W. Foley Middle East Fellowship for early-career freelance journalists (1-5 years' experience), a distinct journalism fellowship encountered while researching CPJ's own James W. Foley Fellowship.

candidates.name: James W. Foley Legacy Foundation
candidates.why: Co-funds/supports CPJ's James W. Foley Fellowship and other journalist-safety fellowship programmes; not currently tracked as its own source.

candidates.name: Canal France International (CFI)
candidates.why: Runs recurring calls for Moldovan and other Eastern Partnership independent media countering disinformation, surfaced via gfmd-fundings but not tracked as its own funder source.

candidates.name: Durham University / Reuters (Sir Harry Evans Global Fellowship)
candidates.why: Co-funds a nine-month investigative fellowship inside a Reuters newsroom, surfaced via gfmd-fellowships but not tracked as its own funder source.

candidates.name: Nova Media / Nova Institute for Health
candidates.why: Funds a health-journalism fellowship for US print/digital/broadcast journalists and nonprofit newsrooms, surfaced via gfmd-fellowships but not tracked as its own funder source.

candidates.name: Exile Hub / Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT)
candidates.why: Jointly runs the Critical Voices Fellowship for exiled Myanmar media professionals, surfaced via gfmd-fellowships but not tracked as its own funder source.

candidates.name: AP Fund for Journalism
candidates.why: A charitable fund created by the Associated Press (2024) providing AP content, editorial tools and training directly to local/state nonprofit newsrooms; surfaced repeatedly while researching Knight Foundation, which has committed $25M to it. Distinct funder/programme not currently tracked as its own source.

candidates.name: Inspirit Foundation — Journalism Futures Fund
candidates.why: New CAD 3.15 million pooled fund (with the Euphrosine, McConnell and Sonor foundations) giving three-year grants to small independent Canadian newsrooms serving underrepresented communities.
candidates.evidence: Inspirit Foundation's own announcement (inspiritfoundation.org, Sept 2025 launch, Feb 2026 inaugural winners) and futureofgood.co coverage of the four-foundation pooled fund. Read October 2026.

candidates.name: The Fund for American Studies (TFAS) — Journalism Excellence Fellowship
candidates.why: New 2026 fellowship placing early-career journalists for 9-12 months in US newsrooms including The Washington Post, The Boston Globe, The Economist and The Dispatch.
candidates.evidence: tfas.org launch announcement, "TFAS launches new Journalism Excellence Fellowship Program". Read October 2026.

candidates.name: African Union Media Fellowship (AUMF)
candidates.why: Pan-African fellowship run by the AU Commission's Information and Communication Directorate, funding training, mentorship and reporting resources for African journalists and content creators continent-wide.
candidates.evidence: au.int press releases on the AUMF 3.0 call and fireside chat, and the fellowship's own site aumf.au.int. Read October 2026.

candidates.name: CORRECTIV (CORRECTIV.Exile)
candidates.why: German investigative newsroom running a recurring, twice-yearly paid residency in Berlin for exiled journalists.

candidates.name: The New York Times (Newsroom Fellowship Program)
candidates.why: Runs an annual paid early-career fellowship for journalists authorized to work in the US/UK; a major, recurring opportunity not currently tracked as its own dedicated funder source.

candidates.name: SEECheck Network
candidates.why: Regional fact-checking network offering short-term grants (EUR 5,000-12,000, 3-6 months) to CSOs and media outlets fighting disinformation in Southeast Europe.

candidates.name: Transitions Media (Building Resilient Journalism Program)
candidates.why: Runs a programme combating disinformation in Southeast Europe through journalism training and direct support for news production debunking disinformation.

candidates.name: Danida (Denmark)
candidates.why: Danish bilateral development cooperation. Media and civil society money is allocated country by country through embassies rather than through open calls, so a newsroom rarely applies directly.

candidates.name: Irish Aid
candidates.why: Irish bilateral aid with a governance strand; country-level discretion rather than published calls.

candidates.name: Austrian Development Agency (ADA)
candidates.why: Austrian development agency with a standing Western Balkans programme, which makes it more relevant to this region than most bilateral donors.

candidates.name: BMZ / develoPPP (Germany)
candidates.why: German development ministry programme with a real application route, though aimed at private-sector partnerships rather than media.

candidates.name: Polish Development Cooperation (Polska Pomoc)
candidates.why: Polish bilateral aid, active in the Eastern Partnership.

candidates.name: RoAid (Romania)
candidates.why: Romanian development cooperation agency, active in the Western Balkans and the Eastern Partnership.

candidates.name: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA)
candidates.why: Japanese grant aid, allocated government to government.

candidates.name: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA)
candidates.why: Korean development agency.

candidates.name: LuxDev (Luxembourg)
candidates.why: Luxembourg development cooperation; publishes tenders rather than grant calls.

candidates.name: New Zealand MFAT aid programme
candidates.why: New Zealand development programme.

candidates.name: KR Foundation
candidates.why: Climate and sustainability funder. Its funding page did not answer an automated check, so the URL needs confirming by hand before this becomes a source.

candidates.name: EU Neighbours East
candidates.why: EU opportunities portal for the Eastern Partnership, which would be directly useful. The page did not answer an automated check and needs confirming.

candidates.name: Media Forward Fund
candidates.why: A transnational fund (launched July 2024, ~EUR 9m, backed by Allianz Foundation, ERSTE Foundation, Rudolf Augstein Stiftung and others) making grants up to EUR 400,000 to media organisations in Germany/Austria/Switzerland for public-interest journalism and sustainable business models.

candidates.name: Springer Nature (Nature Middle East)
candidates.why: Co-funds/partners with MIT's Knight Science Journalism Program on the Fellowship for Advancing Science Journalism in Africa and the Middle East, created in memory of its former Nature Middle East editor Mohammed Yahia.

candidates.name: Cyrus R. Vance Center for International Justice
candidates.why: Co-founded Reporters Shield with OCCRP, providing the legal infrastructure behind the mutual-defense membership programme for investigative newsrooms.

candidates.name: Institute for Nonprofit News (INN)
candidates.why: Appears to administer or fiscally sponsor the Reporters Shield mutual-defense fund membership programme for nonprofit newsrooms, per third-party coverage.

candidates.name: Bard College Center for Ethics and Writing
candidates.why: Co-runs, with Artists at Risk Connection (PEN America), a one-year non-residency fellowship providing direct support to writers and artists whose free expression is threatened.

candidates.name: Booth Ferris Foundation
candidates.why: Named as the funder behind the Bard College/ARC Center for Ethics and Writing Program Fellowship; no public grants-application website found.

candidates.name: EU Commission Fund for Exiled and Relocated Journalists (DG CNECT)
candidates.why: A separate EU Commission call (third round, ~EUR 3 million) for exiled journalists from Belarus/Russia and relocated Ukrainian journalists, open to public authorities/NGOs/research centres; most recent window (16 Apr-28 May 2026) is now closed. Distinct from both JX Fund and EED, and not currently in sources.json.

candidates.name: Open Society Institute – Sofia (OSI-Sofia)
candidates.why: A regional OSF national entity running its own Europe-specific (Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Hungary, Slovenia) media-resilience call, distinct from the global Open Society Foundations programme already tracked as the 'osf' source.

candidates.name: Civil Society Fund (Slovenia)
candidates.why: EEA/Norway Grants-backed Slovenian NGO fund (organisational grants call, deadline 15 Oct 2026) seen today via gfmd-fundings; broader than journalism specifically (media literacy is one of several themes) so not recorded as a grant, but logged as a candidate funder to watch.

candidates.name: DFRLab (Digital Forensic Research Lab, Atlantic Council)
candidates.why: Runs Digital Sherlocks, the only genuine opportunity found in today's stale ijnet-opportunities feed; DFRLab is not itself one of the eight tracked sources.

candidates.name: Goethe-Institut — Innovation. Media. Minds. (EU-funded Western Balkans media grants)
candidates.why: EU-funded media grants (up to EUR 30,000, projects up to 8 months) for independent media across Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia, run by Goethe-Institut with DW Akademie; the current round closed 18 September 2025, found while searching for a successor to eu-delegation-serbia's closed media call.

candidates.name: GIZ / DW Akademie — Sustain Media (EU & BMZ-funded Western Balkans media grants)
candidates.why: EU and German BMZ-funded grants (EUR 10,000-80,000) to establish Media Resource Centers supporting small/local media outlets in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia; the most recent round's deadline (15 March 2026) has passed, found while searching for a successor to eu-delegation-serbia's closed media call.

candidates.name: EU Civil Society Facility and Media Programme (Western Balkans & Türkiye, 2025-2027 multiannual action plan)
candidates.why: A regional EU multi-country mechanism for civil-society and media grants covering the Western Balkans (including Serbia) and Türkiye under a financing decision adopted June 2025 for 2025-2027; no confirmed Serbia-specific call date found yet, so worth re-checking in future sweeps.

candidates.name: European Fund for the Balkans (EFB) — Engaged Democracy Initiative / Opportunity & Innovation Grants
candidates.why: Independent regional grantmaker covering the Western Balkans (including Serbia); its listings include small regional investigative-journalism grants (deadline already passed) and 'Opportunity & Innovation Grants' tagged for media & journalism with an aggregator-reported but unverified deadline of 2 November 2026 — worth checking directly on the funder's own site.

candidates.name: NIAS Safe Haven Fellowship (Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study)
candidates.why: A fellowship explicitly open to journalists (alongside scholars, artists and writers) unable to work in their current location due to conflict or war, with relocation, stipend and travel support, surfaced while researching Scholars at Risk's journalist-placement options.

candidates.name: Massey College Journalism Fellowships (William Southam Fellowship / Gordon N. Fisher-JHR Fellowship)
candidates.why: A Canadian journalism fellowship programme, including one specifically for journalists from Sub-Saharan Africa or the Middle East, surfaced while researching Scholars at Risk's academic/journalist placement pathways.

candidates.name: MEdIA-Lit
candidates.why: Media-literacy and local-media grant programme for Western Balkans CSOs and outlets, run by the Center for Civic Cooperation (CGO), surfaced while researching the EU's Western Balkans/Türkiye Civil Society Facility and Media Programme.

candidates.name: EaP Civil Society Facility (fellowships)
candidates.why: A separate, Eastern Partnership-specific civil society facility (distinct from the Western Balkans one) running its own fellowship/regrant cycles, e.g. a 'Civil Society Resilience' cohort.

candidates.name: OGP Civil Society Innovations for Open Government / EU4Integrity
candidates.why: EU-funded grants specifically for Eastern Partnership CSOs (Armenia, Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine) for public-engagement/open-government tools, with a possible public-information/documentation angle worth separate evaluation.

candidates.name: Global Strategic Communications Council
candidates.why: A dedicated climate-communications funding vehicle co-funded by the European Climate Foundation and the Hewlett Foundation; potentially closer to a journalism/media-communications fit than ECF's core, invite-only grantmaking.

candidates.name: Heartefact / Culture for Democracy Serbia
candidates.why: Swiss-embassy-funded cultural job-shadowing fund in Serbia (all cultural/artistic sectors); weak fit for journalism specifically but borderline-relevant if it ever covers media-arts documentation.

candidates.name: ARTICLE 19 Europe
candidates.why: Named today as an implementing partner of the Media Freedom Rapid Response consortium providing legal/advocacy support to journalists in danger; worth checking whether it runs its own dedicated grants or emergency-support scheme.

candidates.name: European Federation of Journalists (EFJ)
candidates.why: Named today as the MFRR consortium partner that coordinates safety and digital-security training offers for journalists; a WebSearch today found past one-off trainings and a current EC-funded master-class project but no standing fund, so it is flagged as a candidate rather than given its own grant entry.

candidates.name: Prague Civil Society Centre
candidates.why: Leads the EU-funded Free Media Hub EAST / Media Freedom Hub re-granting consortium and runs its own direct media grants (average ~€64,000) for independent outlets across Eastern Europe, the South Caucasus and Central Asia.

candidates.name: Women's Peace and Humanitarian Fund (WPHF)
candidates.why: UN multi-partner trust fund making rolling direct-support (up to USD 30,000) and short-term (up to USD 100,000) grants to women-led civil society organisations and informal women's networks in ODA-eligible countries engaged in peace processes; its country and thematic calls periodically include public-facing awareness/communications components, which could plausibly cover women-led media or documentation work depending on the specific round.

candidates.name: World Press Institute Fellowship
candidates.why: Surfaced in aggregator results alongside GIJN-adjacent 2026 journalism-grant roundups; not confirmed as actually listed on GIJN's own page, lower confidence - flagged for human verification before adding as a tracked source.

candidates.name: Knight-Bagehot Fellowship in Economics and Business Journalism (Columbia Journalism School)
candidates.why: Surfaced in the same aggregator roundup as a business/economics-journalism fellowship comparable to the already-tracked McGraw Fellowship; not confirmed as listed directly on GIJN's own page - flagged for human verification before adding.

candidates.name: Investigative Reporters and Editors (IRE) — Freelance Fellowship
